# Independent audit: truncated entropy and convex hinge repair

Audited all five sections of
truncated-relative-entropy-convex-hinge-repair-root.md.
Result: PASS within its explicit discounted-coupling and actual-branch
hypotheses. No OC payment is inferred.

1. The bounded-dual-parameter global extension is finite convex because
   its q coefficient is nonnegative. On C, an active affine denominator
   and the true maximizing t attain the same value; every other candidate
   is bounded above by it. This avoids the failed unrestricted
   q log(q/L) composition for convex hinges.
2. Joint scalar convexity gives the endpoint-average lower bound, and
   monotonicity in q permits replacing q_bar by q_mid. The remaining
   difference can also be written exactly as

       integral_V^Lmid (q_mid/t-1)_+ dt.

   It is at least (q_mid-Lmid)_+ log(Lmid/V), including either branch
   crossing and all zero-weight cases. Hence the pointwise discounted
   error inequality has the stated sign and exact coefficient d.
3. The error measure is the SAME already selected coupling's error.
   Its integrated F Jensen gap decreases by convex order, while
   T=integral(q-L)_+ drho is bounded ABOVE by the fixed endpoint budget
   through midpoint Jensen. Although convex order increases T relative
   to the old law, the proof never uses the opposite claim. The function
   T(1-exp(-d Delta/T)) increases in both variables; its T derivative is
   1-exp(-x)(1+x)>=0. Thus the nonlinear estimate follows correctly.
4. For q=k h, direct expansion gives the stated uniform remainder in
   [0,U/k]. At kh<=L it is (L/k)t(1-log t), with t in [0,1], indeed in
   that interval. Consequently the integrated remainder is bounded in
   absolute value by mU/k. The coefficient of log k is exactly the
   old hinge Jensen gap, not an unsigned cap probability difference.
5. For opposite endpoint margin signs, that gap is exactly one half
   of the smaller absolute margin; direct cases verify the coefficient.
   If its integral vanishes, pointwise nonnegativity gives zero old
   crossing almost everywhere. Convex order plus midpoint Jensen gives
   zero new crossing too. The zero-gap limit passes uniformly and gives
   the stated finite bound. If the gap is positive the logarithmic cost
   diverges, so the note correctly makes no free cap-localization claim.

All boundary conventions, zero-mass cases, finite global tests, parity
assembly factors and distinctions between actual branch measures and
arbitrary self-pairing are retained. No repair identified.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
